title: Shelf publisher onramp: slate + acceptance checks (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working slate for quick publisher onboarding to the cloud shelf (aka marketplace tile). Focus: minimum acceptance checks so a partner/publisher can go from sign-up -> tile publish with minimal engineering friction. Use this as a lab-first checklist (not final legal-signed contract).

Scope & audience:
- Internal: GTM + Partner Ops + Publisher engineering + Solutions engineers.
- External: ISV/publishers that want to list Redwood-hosted SKU(s) or integrate private/dedicated offers.
- Not in scope: full commercial contracting, enterprise-only marketplace variants (separate runbook).

High-level onboarding flow (short):
1) Intake form -> basic metadata + contact + technical readiness answers.
2) Quick security self-attest (low-risk publishers skip deep review).
3) Asset drop: tile copy + two screenshots + 30s video (optional).
4) QA smoke tests in sandbox (auth, basic API call, telemetry).
5) Internal review (comms, legal flags, pricing SKU mapping).
6) Publish to staging -> smoke -> publish to production shelf.

Acceptance checklist (working, minimal viable):
- Identity & contacts: primary contact, technical contact, billing contact (email addresses)
- Tile copy delivered: short description (<= 140 chars), long description (<= 800 chars), 3 bullets of key benefits, call-to-action
- Screenshots: 2 x 1280x720 PNGs (no PII)
- Logo: SVG (square + 1:3 horizontal) and small PNG 160x160
- SKU mapping: single SKU id, pricing model (usage/per-embed/per-token), free tier ? (yes/no)
- Entitlements & trial: trial length, trial cap per tenant, renewal flow described
- API integration test: sample API key works in sandbox, returns status 200 and expected schema
- Telemetry: events and dimensions defined for 1) install, 2) trial start, 3) conversion, 4) API error rate
- Privacy & data residency note: boolean if customer data leaves region (yes/no)
- Basic security attestation: OWASP checklist tickbox, dependencies declared
- Legal pre-check: permitted usecases (no regulated health/finance unless flagged)
- Accessibility: alt text for images provided
- Accessibility: minimal landing copy conforms to WCAG basic readability (note if not)

Detailed required assets (deliverables):
- Copy:
  - Hero short (1 line): e.g., "Embed Redwood Inference for fast, production-grade LLM inference" (publisher should provide variant)
  - 140-char elevator pitch
  - 3 bullet feature/value bullets (user-facing benefits)
  - 3-4 technical bulleted notes for integration page (auth, endpoints, rate limits, zones)
- Images & media:
  - 2 screenshots + 1 logo SVG + 1 PNG small
  - Optional 30s demo video (mp4, <= 50MB)
- Technical:
  - Sandbox API key + sample curl/SDK snippet
  - Sample response JSON schema (trimmed)
  - Error codes mapping (400/401/403/429/5xx semantics)
- Billing:
  - SKU id, metering dimensions (tokens, inference-units, embeddings), price bands (if tiered), free tier limits
- Compliance:
  - Data handling statement (does vendor store user input? retention?)
  - Contact for security when published

Telemetry & instrumentation (must-haves):
- Required events: publisher_install, trial_start, trial_conversion, api_call_success, api_call_error, rate_limit_hit
- Dimensions: partner_id, region, sku_id, tenant_id (when applicable), env (staging/prod)
- Error reporting schema example: {"event": "api_call_error", "code": "RATE_LIMIT", "latency_ms": "120"}  <- publisher to supply mapping (we expect JSON events; we will adapt logs on ingestion)
- Sample dashboard KPIs for partner team: installs/week, conversions, avg latency, 95th latency, token consumption/day, error rate

Copy snippets (editable drafts) - publisher should refine tone of voice to Redwood style but allowed to use their branding: 
- Hero short (140): "Add fast, cost-aware LLM inference to your app with Redwood-hosted publisher integrations."
- Long (<=800): "[Publisher] lets product teams add LLM features without babysitting infrastructure. Through a Redwood-hosted tile, customers get a pre-configured endpoint, usage plans, and a simple meter-and-bill experience. Integration is a few lines of code: API key + call. Trials included."
- Feature bullets (user-facing):
  - "Ready-to-use endpoints: pre-tuned configs for latency/cost tradeoffs."
  - "Transparent metering and billing: pay only for usage; trial quotas included."
  - "Secure by default: isolation options for Dedicated and Private deployments."
- Technical bullets (integration):
  - "Auth: API key in header X-Redwood-Key; endpoints: api.redwood.ai/publishers/{sku}/infer"
  - "Rate limits: default 60 rps per key; burst policies available via request"
  - "Regions: US-EAST, EU-WEST, APAC coming Q4"

Onboarding gating logic (how we decide fast-track vs full review):
- Fast-track (auto-approve): single-SKU, free-tier only, no external PII handling, publisher security attestation signed, images and copy correct.
- Full review: multiple SKUs with custom pricing, handles regulated data, requires enterprise SSO or VPC connectors, or references unusual dependencies.

Common friction points (notes from se/ops):
- Missing SKU mapping (vendor uses internal SKUs) -> ask them to provide 1:1 mapping or we create a marketplace SKU on their behalf.
- Incomplete telemetry -> requires follow-up to avoid blind spots in usage reporting
- Pricing ambiguity -> push for clear per-unit pricing; avoid vague "contact us" unless enterprise only

Open questions & TODOs:
- Who signs the final marketplace contract? (legal/team: determine if Redwood or publisher signs for billing terms)
- Mapping for legacy publisher plans -> transform rules needed (example rules TBD)
- Should we require vulnerability scan for all publishers or only high-risk? Proposed: only high-risk for MVP.
- SLA language: do we bake a 99.5% tile SLA or leave to publisher-managed? (ops/infra to advise)

Next steps (owners):
- Priya: finalize intake form fields and hand to Ops (due 2024-10-10)
- Marco: prototype staging tile and automated smoke test harness (due 2024-10-17)
- Alina: legal quick-check template (due 2024-10-14)
- SE on call: Samir (first publisher trial)

Reviewer checklist before publish to prod:
- All assets present + copy approved by comms
- Sandbox smoke tests pass (auth, response schema, telemetry sent)
- SKU and pricing mapped and pushed to billing test harness
- Legal flags cleared or escrowed with publisher
- Accessibility alt text present
- Owner sign-off (GTM owner + SE + Ops)

Notes to self / friction log (scratchpad tone):
- Keep intake form under 10 fields. Long forms = drop-off for early-stage publishers.
- Consider a lighter "badge" program for very small ISVs to reduce overhead.
- Track time-from-intake->publish for first 5 pubs and refine flow.

Links & references (internal):
- Confluence quick spec: confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTM/Publisher+Shelf+Onramp
- Jira epic: GTM-912
- Example published tile to emulate: redwood-inference-public/tiles/sample-connector (internal repo)

End of scratchpad.
